proposal.original_claim_summary: The entry says executive orders and funding freezes effectively disbanded the CFPB in August 2025 and dropped all pending enforcement actions.

identified_problems.explanation: The major stop-work, dismissal and attempted mass-layoff actions began in February and April 2025, not August 12.
The record combines a February work halt and initial dismissals, later partial resumption under litigation, and an April attempt to dismiss most of the workforce.

The CFPB was not legally disbanded; courts halted or constrained mass layoffs and some legally required work resumed. The claim that all pending enforcement actions were dropped is broader than the evidence reviewed.

proposed_split_entries.proposed_title: Trump administration halts much CFPB work and begins staff reductions
proposed_split_entries.proposed_synopsis: Acting CFPB leadership ordered broad work stoppages and the administration began terminating categories of employees in February 2025, prompting litigation from the employees' union.

proposed_split_entries.proposed_title: CFPB attempts to lay off roughly 90% of workforce; judge halts dismissals
proposed_split_entries.proposed_synopsis: The CFPB attempted to dismiss roughly 1,400 to 1,500 employees in April, potentially eliminating about 90% of the agency's workforce. A federal judge halted the mass firings while litigation over compliance with earlier court orders continued.

proposed_split_entries.proposed_title: Some CFPB work resumes amid court challenge
proposed_split_entries.proposed_synopsis: Emails showed that the administration allowed several CFPB offices to resume functions officials considered legally required, undercutting the claim that the agency had simply ceased to exist.

claims.claim: The administration attempted sweeping CFPB staff reductions and work stoppages beginning in February 2025.
An April 2025 attempt to lay off roughly 90% of the CFPB workforce was halted by a federal judge.
The CFPB was legally disbanded in August 2025 and all enforcement matters were dropped.
claims.notes: The agency remained in existence and litigation preserved some functions and staff.

proposal.original_claim_summary: Trump Draws Electoral College Map With Sharpie to Inflate Victory
proposal.original_synopsis: Shortly after taking office, Trump reportedly showed visitors to the Oval Office a doctored Electoral College map drawn with Sharpie that expanded his red states to make his 2016 electoral victory appear larger than it was. The map was allegedly shown to visitors on multiple occasions as a prop demonstrating his historic victory. Election experts and cartographers noted the alterations misrepresented the actual electoral geography. The episode pre-dated the more famous Sharpiegate hurricane incident but reflected the same pattern of using a Sharpie to alter official documents or representations. The incident reinforced concerns about Trump's obsessive need to appear more successful than the actual record showed.

frozen_original.title: Trump Fires Inspector General Who Investigated DOJ Political Interference
frozen_original.synopsis: On January 20, 2025, Trump fired the Department of Justice Inspector General — the independent watchdog responsible for investigating misconduct, fraud, and political interference within DOJ — as part of a mass firing of more than a dozen inspectors general across the federal government. The DOJ IG had been overseeing investigations into improper political influence on DOJ prosecutions and had previously documented political interference during Trump's first term. The mass firing of inspectors general — who are protected by statute from removal without cause and congressional notification — was challenged in court by the fired officials and condemned by the Government Accountability Office and congressional oversight committees. The elimination of internal DOJ oversight ensured that political manipulation of federal prosecution decisions could proceed without independent accountability, completing the conversion of the Justice Department into an instrument of political power.
